title: Overriding cannot reduce method visibility
answer: No. An overriding method cannot reduce the accessibility of the inherited method. If the parent method is protected, the override must remain protected or become public; package-private access would be weaker and causes a compile-time error. This preserves substitutability because callers that are allowed to invoke the parent contract must not lose that access merely because the runtime object is a subclass.
